why: A national bill-printing firm with about $24m monthly revenue from about 41m items (around $0.60 per item), and profit equal to revenue minus costs in both columns, is believable.
A packaging supplier with roughly $1bn revenue and about a 17% share of each segment's market, with 60-200 reps bringing in $3-6.5m each, is believable for B2B packaging sales.
Converting a harvest weight in kilograms to bushels and pricing it per bushel is a sensible premise with no figures that could be wrong.
Twelve studios with 8 to 67 architects and $1m to $16m revenue each (about $77m from 350 architects, roughly $220k per architect) is believable for an architecture practice.
An online beauty retailer whose shoppers place 1.2 to 6.6 orders worth about $47-$63 each in 90 days and earn it $1.50-$31 profit a year is believable, if thin-margin.
Every rating distribution sums to 100% and the 30,000 plus 18,000 users match the 48,000 total, so the survey data is consistent.
About 1.3 million employees in a home region, split across groups and employer sizes with managers about a fifth of staff, is believable.
A florist whose orders roughly double before Mother's Day, with agency hours rising from about 8% to 45% of total hours, is believable.
